conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you came in today after feeling lightheaded and sweaty while walking with your sister this morning?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, that’s right. Out of nowhere I started sweating a lot, felt shaky, and had to lie down. It lasted about 15 minutes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And you mentioned some chest pain and a fluttering in your neck?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Just for a minute or two—felt like my heart was jumping. But no chest pain now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Your vitals were stable when you arrived. We ran some tests because we wanted to rule out serious causes like a blood clot or heart issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I was worried it was my heart again. I just got out of the hospital two days ago.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know. You were treated for heart failure and pneumonia. Your chest X-ray today shows the lung infection is improving. No signs of a pulmonary embolism on the CT scan either.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what caused the episode then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s not completely clear. Your EKG and heart enzymes were normal. The sweating and lightheadedness could be from low blood pressure—your systolic was 98 when you got here, down from the 130s when you left the hospital.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Could it be my heart racing again? I felt that flutter.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possible. You have atrial fibrillation, and your home dose of metoprolol is lower than what you were on in the hospital—200mg instead of 300mg—because of insurance issues. That might have let your heart rate go up briefly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I couldn’t refill the full dose yet. Insurance said it wasn’t time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That could be part of it. Also, your blood sugar was 125—normal now—but symptoms improved after you ate, so a temporary low sugar might have played a role.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I hadn’t eaten breakfast before we went walking.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. We’re keeping an eye on your heart and lungs. You’re on your usual COPD inhalers, and we gave you another dose of methadone this morning—you were set up at the clinic, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I got 40mg yesterday. I missed my dose the day before—got there too late. But I got it today, so that’s good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We sent a note to the clinic so they know you got your dose here. We were also going to adjust your clonazepam since it’s hard to get refills, but we’ll discuss that later.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your repeat labs look stable—kidney function is fine, no signs of infection worsening. Your lungs are clear on exam now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel okay now. No dizziness or chest stuff.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Glad to hear it. We still need to talk about your medications and follow-up, especially your heart and methadone treatment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I understand, but I need to get to the clinic for my dose. I don’t want to miss another one.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We already gave you 40mg this morning, and we’ve notified the clinic. You’re all set for today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. Thanks. I think I’m going to head out then. I feel fine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’d really prefer you stay a bit longer so we can go over your care plan. Your symptoms could come back if we don’t address the medication issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate it, doc, but I’ve got to go. I’ll follow up with my doctors.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Alright. Just know we’re concerned about your heart rate control and access to meds. Please see your cardiologist and addiction clinic as soon as possible.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for the help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’re sending a summary to your clinics. Please don’t hesitate to come back if symptoms return.
